title: Controlled vocabulary
description: One file per open vocabulary used by an entity field: data/vocab/<id>.json, published verbatim at v1/vocab/<id>.json. Gives every code a human label and description so a consumer can render any value it encounters and fail visibly (not silently) on a code it does not recognize. `applies_to` names the entity field(s) this vocabulary governs; `open: true` means new codes may appear over time, so consumers should tolerate unknowns. tools/validate_data.py checks that every code actually used in the data appears here.

applies_to.description: Entity field(s) this vocabulary governs, e.g. 'camp.program_types'.

open.description: true = new codes may be added over time; consumers should tolerate unknown codes.

category.description: What KIND of thing the term is, so a consumer can group terms without hardcoding them: a facility (dining_hall), an activity (climbing), a program/enrollment model (provisional attendance), an accommodation attribute (cabin housing, step-free access), or a subject area (stem). Optional — a vocabulary governing a single kind may omit it.

broader.description: Optional parent term in this same vocabulary, so specific leaves answer coarse queries (sailing -> aquatics). tools/validate_data.py rejects an unknown parent, a self-reference, and any cycle.

aliases.description: Synonyms this term absorbs so an open vocabulary does not fork (atv <- quads, four_wheeling). Aliases are NOT valid values in data — they exist to be mapped onto `code` during curation. tools/validate_data.py rejects an alias colliding with any term's code or with another term's alias.
